actions.name: create_response
actions.description:
Create Response. Generate a model reply in the OpenAI Responses format.

**Models:** `sarvam-105b`, `glm5.3`, `gemma4`, and `deepseekv4.1-flash` (ids are case-sensitive).

**Each call is independent.** Send the full conversation in `input` every time — nothing is stored for you. Leave out `store` or set it to `false` (`true` returns **`400`**). You cannot load a past response by id (`GET /v2/responses/{id}` is always **`404`**).

**Streaming is optional.** Default is a single JSON body (`stream` omitted or `false`). Set `stream: true` only if you want server-sent events.

**Reasoning (`glm5.3`, `deepseekv4.1-flash`):** both support `low`, `high`, and `max`. On `glm5.3`, `reasoning.effort`...

model.description:
Model IDs accepted by `POST /v2/responses` (case-sensitive; unknown ids return `404`):

- **`sarvam-105b`** — Sarvam flagship model.
- **`glm5.3`** — 1,048,576-token context; reasoning in `output` as a `reasoning` item; flat function tools; max request size 10,485,760 bytes.
- **`gemma4`** — vision (inline base64 images) and tools.
- **`deepseekv4.1-flash`** — long context, tools, and reasoning.

input.description: A prompt string, or the conversation so far as a list of items. Replay the full list on every request because this endpoint does not store prior turns.

items.description: A message (has `role`) or a pass-through protocol item such as `function_call`, `function_call_output`, or `reasoning`. `item_reference` is `400`.

role.description: One of `user`, `assistant`, `system`, `developer`. Any other role is `400`.

content.description: A string, or an array of content parts. Assistant `output_text` / `input_text` parts are flattened to one string on the way out. A non-text part on an assistant turn is `400`.

items.description: an object (see the provider's API docs)

type.description: Optional. Messages may omit this; OpenAI often sends `message`.

anyOf.description: A protocol item that is not a modelled message — `function_call`, `function_call_output`, `reasoning`, and anything the protocol adds later. `item_reference` is `400` (inline the item in `input` instead). Other types are forwarded as sent. Image rules still run over the outbound payload, so an `input_image` nested in `function_call_output` is refused on the same terms.

stream.description: Optional. Default `false` — same as chat completions. Omit or `false` for one JSON response body. Set `true` to stream named server-sent events. There is no `[DONE]` sentinel — the stream ends on `response.completed`, `response.incomplete`, or `response.failed`.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens to generate, including reasoning tokens on reasoning models. If omitted, there is no default cap — generation is unbounded and continues until the model stops on its own or the context window fills. Always set this explicitly in production. Values above the model context window return `400`.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Default **`1`** on `glm5.3` when omitted. Output is not bit-reproducible, even at `0`.

store.description: Must be `false` or omitted (omitting is `200` and echoed as `false`). `true` is `400 invalid_request_error` — nothing created here is retrievable. OpenAI SDKs default this to `true`, so a default `client.responses.create(...)` fails.

tools.description: Function tools use the **flat** Responses shape (`type`, `name`, `parameters`, `strict`) — the nested chat-completions tool shape is **`400`**. `tool_choice: required` with no tools returns **`400`**. Function `arguments` in output are a JSON **string** (parse before use). Multiple tool calls per turn are supported; use **`parallel_tool_calls: true`** or omit (see that field).

name.description: The function name.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the function arguments.

tool_choice.description: Forwarded exactly as written: `none`, `auto`, `required`, `{ "type": "function", "name": "..." }`, or another object.

anyOf.description: Forwarded exactly as written: `none`, `auto`, `required`, `{ "type": "function", "name": "..." }`, or another object.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

On `glm5.3`, a reasoning item is always in `output` — read `summary[0].text`. **`effort`:** on `glm5.3`, `low` or `high` only — omit for `max`-level reasoning (the literal string `max` returns `400`); on `deepseekv4.1-flash`, `low`, `high`, or `max` all work directly. Optional **`summary`:** `auto` or `detailed`.

n.description: **Ignored** on this route — Responses always returns one output. Accepted for OpenAI SDK compatibility only; omit or leave at `1`.

seed.description: **Ignored** on Responses. Accepted for SDK compatibility only.

**Base URL:** `https://api.sarvam.ai/dubbing`.
**Auth:** send your key in the `api-subscription-key` header, not `Authorization: Bearer`.

2. `POST /jobs/{job_id}/s...

target_langs.description: One or more target languages to dub into. A single job dubs into all of them.

items.description: Supported BCP-47 language code for dubbing. Note: Odia is `or-IN` for the dubbing service.

export_options.description: Which formats to auto-produce per target language. When provided, only the listed formats are auto-exported. Start Dubbing Job. Start a dubbing job once the media file has been uploaded to the signed `upload_url` returned by `POST /jobs`. The job status then moves from `queued` to `in_progress`, and finally to `completed` or `failed`.

The audio file to transcribe. Supported formats include WAV, MP3, AAC, AIFF, OGG, OPUS, FLAC, MP4/M4A, AMR, WMA, WebM, and PCM formats. The API automatically detects most codec formats, but for PCM files (pcm_s16le, pcm_l16, pcm_raw), you must specify the input_audio_codec parameter. PCM files are supported only at 16kHz sample rate.
